metadata.title: Troy Franklin Playing a Minimal Role on Offense
metadata.description: Denver Broncos wide receiver Troy Franklin has taken a massive step back in 2026, dropping him off the fantasy radar in most leagues. The Broncos' offseason addition of Jaylen Waddle seems to have spelled disaster for Franklin, who has just one catch through two weeks and has yet to play more than 33% of the snaps in a single game this season. In addition to Waddle, both Courtland Sutton and Pat Bryant have also consistently played more than Franklin, which means he's down to the fourth rung on the depth chart. The 23-year-old has a rapport with quarterback Bo Nix dating back to their time at Oregon, so maybe he still has some potential long-term. However, in the short term, he's going to remain buried on the depth chart, keeping him off the fantasy radar.

metadata.title: Troy Franklin - One catch in Week 2 win
metadata.description: Franklin caught one of two targets for 27 yards in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Jaguars.
metadata.analysis: With Marvin Mims (foot) inactive, Franklin played 13 of 62 offensive snaps as the clear No. 4 receiver behind Courtland Sutton, Pat Bryant and Jaylen Waddle. Franklin's 27-yard grab was his lone catch of the season through two weeks. He'll need an injury to obtain any fantasy relevance in redraft formats.

metadata.title: Troy Franklin (knee) good to go for Sunday
metadata.description: Troy Franklin (knee) will be good to go for Sunday's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars.
metadata.analysis: Franklin found himself on the injury report earlier in the week due to a knee issue, but he was able to practice in full all week and will be good to go for Sunday's game against the Jaguars. He isn't expected to be fantasy relevant for the foreseeable future, however.

metadata.title: Troy Franklin Enduring a Massive Dip in Volume
metadata.description: Denver Broncos wide receiver Troy Franklin is quickly losing the fantasy stock that he worked hard to earn last season. Franklin finished the 2025 season as the overall WR31 in PPR leagues with over 100 targets and six touchdowns. Managers knew his fantasy-relevant role was going to be threatened in 2026 after the team traded for Jaylen Waddle, but perhaps everyone underestimated the extent to which Franklin would be taken out of the offense. He played just 33% of the snaps on Monday night, fetching one target (zero receptions). In addition to Waddle, Franklin was out-snapped and out-produced by both Courtland Sutton and Pat Bryant, potentially dropping him to No. 4 on the depth chart. Between his low snap share and the crowded receiver room, Franklin is no longer worth considering for fantasy lineups, starting with Week 2 against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Managers could even justify dropping him in leagues with 10 or fewer teams.

metadata.title: Troy Franklin (knee) fully practices Wednesday
metadata.description: Troy Franklin (knee) fully practiced for the Broncos on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Franklin was added to the injury report due to a knee injury that he is currently dealing with, but he was able to fully practice on Wednesday and seems to be good to go for Week 2. Fantasy managers shouldn't have high hopes for him for the foreseeable future.

metadata.title: Troy Franklin - Quiet performance in Week 1
metadata.description: Franklin failed to reel in his only target while adding a five-yard rush in Monday night's 31-10 loss to Kansas City.
metadata.analysis: Franklin was only on the field for 17 of the team's 51 offensive snaps, which was fewer than Pat Bryant (30) along with starters Courtland Sutton and Jaylen Waddle at wide receiver. The 23-year-old emerged as a go-to option for quarterback Bo Nix in 2025, catching 65 of 104 targets for 709 yards and six scores, but with the addition of Waddle in the offseason, Franklin appears to be locked into a depth role this season.

metadata.title: Troy Franklin doesn't contribute in loss Monday
metadata.description: Troy Franklin failed to catch his lone target and had one rush for five yards in Monday night's 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
metadata.analysis: It was no surprise that Franklin was uninvolved for the Broncos on Monday night, as their offense struggled heavily to get even their best players the ball against the Chiefs. He seems to be squarely behind at least three other wideouts on the depth chart at this point, however, which makes him irrelevant from a fantasy perspective until further notice.

metadata.title: Troy Franklin Could Be Facing a Reduced Role in Crowded WR Room
metadata.description: Denver Broncos wide receiver Troy Franklin put together a pretty productive season in 2025, recording 65 catches for 709 yards and six touchdowns on 106 targets across 17 games (seven starts). However, the 23-year-old's production faded a bit down the stretch, as he averaged fewer than three catches and 30 receiving yards over his final seven games of the year (including the postseason). Franklin's place in the Broncos' wide receiver room is in question entering 2026. The team acquired star wideout Jaylen Waddle, who now looks like the clear WR1 in Denver. Veteran Courtland Sutton should be the team's WR2, and 2025 third-round pick Pat Bryant has drawn rave reviews for his work in Broncos camp this summer. As a result, Franklin may be facing a significantly reduced workload in Denver in 2026.

metadata.title: Troy Franklin - Fails to corral sole target
metadata.description: Franklin failed to secure his only target in the Broncos' 34-6 preseason win over the Vikings on Friday.
metadata.analysis: Franklin opened preseason with a 23-yard grab in the opener against the Falcons, but that turned out to be his only production of the exhibition slate across three games. Despite the quiet summer, Franklin is slated to serve as the No. 3 receiver behind Courtland Sutton and Jaylen Waddle in what should be a high-powered Broncos air attack.

metadata.title: Troy Franklin is No Longer a Flashy Fantasy Target
metadata.description: Denver Broncos wide receiver Troy Franklin fell down the depth chart this past offseason after the team traded for Jaylen Waddle from Miami. Not only did Franklin slip to No. 3 in the wide receiver pecking order, but he hasn't exactly made a compelling case for more volume. In Week 2 of the preseason, he played 16 snaps but didn't fetch a single target. Last year, he was the WR31 in PPR leagues with 709 yards and six touchdowns, but he might have trouble eclipsing those same numbers in his new role behind both Waddle and Courtland Sutton. The good news for Franklin is that his quarterback and former college teammate, Bo Nix (ankle), is back from injury, but we're still not very confident in the 23-year-old receiver for fantasy purposes as long as Waddle and Sutton are healthy. As it stands, Franklin is the WR102 in RotoBaller's latest fantasy football draft rankings for 2026.

metadata.title: Troy Franklin - Silent Friday night
metadata.description: Franklin played 16 offensive snaps in Friday night's preseason game against the Packers, but he did not appear in the box score.
metadata.analysis: Franklin had a short night, but the lack of any targets is not a good showing for the supposed No. 3 wide receiver. With the offseason addition of Jaylen Waddle, Franklin is set to see a regression in target share, so he will need to earn every snap. The speedy Oregon product provides a nice deep threat to complement Waddle, but it remains to be seen how he will be utilized in the new offense.
